header:
Is renting really
throwing money away?

lines.text: Myth: renting is throwing money away.
lines.say: Myth: renting is throwing money away.

lines.text: Owners throw money away too. It's just called something else.
lines.say: Owners throw money away too. It's just called something else.

lines.text: Mortgage interest, property taxes, insurance and repairs never come back to you.
lines.say: Mortgage interest, property taxes, insurance and repairs never come back to you.

lines.text: One popular rule of thumb puts those costs at around 5% of the home's value per year.
lines.say: One popular rule of thumb puts those costs at around five percent of the home's value per year.

scene.label: A rule of thumb for owners' yearly costs
scene.sub: of the home's value (varies a lot)

lines.text: On a 400,000 dollar home, that's about 20,000 dollars a year, or 1,667 a month.
lines.say: On a four hundred thousand dollar home, that's about twenty thousand dollars a year, or sixteen hundred sixty-seven a month.

lines.text: So compare rent to that number, not to the whole mortgage payment. Sometimes renting wins, sometimes buying does.
lines.say: So compare rent to that number, not to the whole mortgage payment. Sometimes renting wins, sometimes buying does.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.
